info.title: Katapatha API
info.description:
Delivery coordination for Waypoint Group. One operation, four role-specific
workspaces: dispatcher, loader, driver, store manager.

## Conventions that are load-bearing

- **Clock times are `"HH:MM"` strings** in Asia/Colombo wall clock, never
  `date-time`. Calendar dates are `date`. The source data carries no
  timezone for times and every rule is expressed in wall-clock minutes, so
  widening these would invent information we do not have.
- **`TempRequirement` (an order needs) and `VehicleTemp` (a vehicle can) are
  different types.** Conflating them is the most common way to break
  feasibility rule 2.
- **Idempotency is part of the contract**, in three places: `requestId` when
  placing orders, `clientRequestId` on a load check, and the client-minted
  ULID that is a `StopEvent`'s primary key.
- **Every mutation enforces ownership**, not just role. A dispatcher is
  scoped to a depot, a store manager to an outlet, a driver to a vehicle.
- **Never imply live vehicle position or background sync.** There is no GPS
  in this system, and offline durability is claimed only once verified.

get.description: The connectivity authority. `navigator.onLine` is a hint only; the driver UI must confirm reachability against this before claiming Connected.

post.description: Sets an httpOnly cookie AND returns a bearer token. Web uses the cookie; the mobile app uses the token. Only a sha256 hash is stored server-side. Throttled per hashed email and IP.

get.summary: The signed-in user and their home route

get.description: Clients render these rather than hardcoding their own copies, so a reason code added on the server appears in web and mobile without a release.

get.summary: The next date the network operates

get.description: A store manager sees their own outlet; a dispatcher sees their depot.

post.summary: Place orders for the next operating day
post.description: Units only. Outlet, brand, district and depot come from the session, never the body. Idempotent on `requestId`, so a retry over a flaky connection cannot double-order.

200.description: Replay of an earlier request with the same `requestId`.

put.summary: Confirm receipt of a delivered order
put.description: Idempotent — one receipt per order, upserted.

get.summary: The order queue state for a date

post.summary: Close the order queue for the day
post.description: OPEN to CLOSED, writing a queue snapshot. Replaying returns 200 with the current state rather than an error — closing twice is not a mistake worth blocking a dispatcher for.

post.summary: Run the allocator and produce a draft plan
post.description: Also the re-run path: an existing DRAFT for the day is replaced, so re-running is free and leaves no trail of half-plans. Requires the planning day to be CLOSED or PLANNING.

deferrals.description: The DEFERRED assignments on this plan, each with the reason code the dispatcher has attached (null when still pending). The dispatcher UI confirms every pending deferral through PUT /plans/{planId}/deferrals before the publication gate opens.

cause.suggestion: fits if VEH003 returns from the workshop

get.summary: Run the shared validator against a plan
get.description: The same isomorphic validator the allocator self-checks with and that publication gates on. Exposing it lets the board show violations live instead of discovering them at publish time.

violations.message: OUT074 was deferred yesterday and is deferred again.

put.summary: Attach a reason code to each deferred order
put.description: Every deferral carries a reason. Publication is blocked while any deferred order lacks one.

get.summary: The other orders competing for a deferred order's lane
get.description: "Why this order and not another." The orders sharing the deferred order's lane (brand + district, the allocator's own grouping), ranked by the same priority policy the allocator used. Read-only; feeds the dispatcher's "Defer order" drawer.

200.description: The deferred order and its competitors.

post.description: An atomic one-time claim. Publishing commits fuel, notifies deferred outlets, and moves served orders to PLANNED. A second attempt is a 409, not a silent success.

get.summary: Published trips at the caller's depot
What to load, in loading order
get.description: Lines come back in REVERSE delivery order, because the driver unloads from the back.

put.description: An upsert, so re-checking a line corrects it rather than duplicating it. A non-OK condition opens a shortfall that blocks departure until resolved.

post.description: Gated: every line must be checked and no open shortfall may block departure. A blocked attempt returns 409 with the specific reason, so the loader can see what is missing rather than a generic failure.

409.description: Blocked by an incomplete load or an open shortfall.

put.summary: Claim a vehicle for the day
put.description: Assignment happens at the dock; it is persisted on the user.

get.summary: Today's run for the claimed vehicle

post.description: All three driver transitions are one endpoint, because they are all just StopEvents. The client mints each event's ULID, so this is idempotent by construction and the offline outbox has exactly one write shape to replay. `duplicate` in the response is a success, not a failure.

The same applier as POST /stops/{stopId}/events, batched and spanning several stops, so the online and offline paths can never diverge. Writes a SyncLog row and measures device clock skew. Replaying an identical batch must report every event as a duplicate and change nothing.

get.summary: Pull events recorded since a sequence number
get.description: Lets a reconnecting device learn about changes it missed, such as a stop reassigned to another vehicle while it was offline.

get.summary: Everything the device must cache to work offline
get.description: One response containing the run plus the reference data a driver needs with no connectivity. Offline durability is only claimed once this and the outbox drain are verified end to end.

bearerAuth.description: Used by the mobile app. Same opaque token as the cookie; only its sha256 hash is stored server-side.

token.description: Opaque bearer token. The same value is also set as an httpOnly cookie. Web uses the cookie; the mobile app uses the bearer token. Only a sha256 hash of this is stored server-side.

examples: You do not own this record.

ClockTime.description: Wall-clock time in Asia/Colombo as "HH:MM". Never a date-time. The source data carries no date and no timezone for times, and every rule in the booklet is expressed in wall-clock minutes, so widening this to date-time would invent information we do not have.

VehicleTemp.description: What a VEHICLE can do. A reefer may carry either; ambient may not carry chilled. Conflating this with TempRequirement is the single most common way to break feasibility rule 2.

Vocabularies.description: Server-owned code lists. Clients must render these rather than hardcoding their own copies, so a reason code added on the server appears everywhere.

DateOnly.description: A calendar date with no time component.

TempRequirement.description: What an ORDER needs. Deliberately distinct from VehicleTemp.

storeState.description: The narrower projection a store manager sees.

deferral.description: Present once a plan that deferred this order is published: the dispatcher's reason and the operating day it moves to. `rolledToDate` is null when no vehicle in the fleet could carry the order as it stands, so no next run is promised. Additive (CONVENTIONS.md rule 8).

PlaceOrdersRequest.description: The store manager supplies units only. Outlet, brand, district and depot are derived server-side from the session — never trusted from the body. Weight and volume are estimated from the outlet's own history.

requestId.description: Idempotency key. Replaying the same requestId returns the original result.

hash.description: Deterministic fingerprint of the allocation. Identical input must always produce an identical hash, so this doubles as a regression guard in CI.

DeferralRow.description: A DEFERRED assignment on a plan. Everything after `reasonCode` is additive and feeds the dispatcher's "Defer order" drawer (Figma D-05).

reasonCode.description: The dispatcher's confirmed reason; null while still pending.

note.description: Free-text note recorded with the reason ("Other · add a note").

cause.description: The allocator's own finding — why no vehicle could take the order.

permanent.description: True when no plan on any day could serve the order as it stands.

examples: fits if VEH003 returns from the workshop

suggestedReasonCode.description: The deferral reason the allocator's finding points at, from the fixed list. Null when the order yielded to a higher-priority one and there is no capacity reason to suggest.

firstOnRun.description: Allocator priority rule 1 — an order deferred yesterday is planned ahead of everything else. First, not guaranteed.

examples: Trip 2 on VEH043 exceeds its volume capacity by 0.8 m³.

overridable.description: Some violations describe a real operational action (recalling a vehicle from the workshop) and may be overridden with a recorded reason. Others never can be: chilled goods on an ambient truck is not a judgement call.

items.description: The deferred order first, then up to four competitors by priority rank.

impact.description: protected — deferred yesterday and served today; skipped_twice — deferred yesterday and deferred again (the HIGH_PRIORITY_DEFERRED warning); lowest — the lowest priority score in the lane; high — the rest.

LoadList.description: Stops are returned in REVERSE delivery order. The driver unloads from the back, so the loader must load the last stop first. This ordering is part of the contract, not a client concern.

checkedByName.description: Typed in per action. The dock terminal is shared between loaders, so the actor cannot be taken from the session.

Ulid.description: Client-generated, time-sortable identifier (Crockford base32). The client mints this so that replaying a write is idempotent by construction.

StopEvent.description: One recorded fact about a stop. The client mints the ULID id, so replaying an event — online or from the offline outbox — is idempotent by construction. `occurredAt` is the DEVICE clock and must be presented as "recorded on device"; the server records its own receipt time separately.

tripStopId.description: Required on the batched POST /sync/stop-events path (a batch spans several stops and the server needs to route each event to the right one). Ignored and may be null on POST /stops/{stopId}/events, where the URL already carries the stop. Additive field; existing clients that omit it keep working on the per-stop path.

status.description: `duplicate` is a success, not an error — it is what a correct outbox replay looks like.

SyncBatchRequest.description: The offline outbox drain. Events may span several stops. This is the same applier as POST /stops/{stopId}/events, batched and unscoped, so the online and offline paths can never diverge.

clientClockAt.description: Device clock at drain time, used to measure skew.

serverSeq.description: Highest server sequence assigned in this batch; use as the next `sinceSeq`.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted. Either the role is wrong, or the record is not owned by this depot, outlet or vehicle.

error.message: You do not own this record.

ValidationFailed.description: The request was well formed but the operation is blocked by business rules. `details.violations` carries the reasons, so the client can render them beside the failed action instead of guessing.

error.message: Two trips exceed their volume capacity.

violations.message: Trip 2 on VEH043 exceeds its volume capacity by 0.8 m³.

NotFound.description: No such record, or not visible at this scope.

Conflict.description: The action does not apply in the record's current state.

error.message: This plan has already been published.

DepotCode.name: depot
DepotCode.description: Depot. Defaults to the caller's own depot; a caller may not read another.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Replaying a request with the same key returns the original response. Reusing a key with a different body is rejected with 422.
